rr6-nx: package notes, what to test on the console
==================================================

Nothing in this package has run on real hardware. Everything below was seen on the PC or in Ryujinx, which are proxies.

Install
-------
Copy COPY_TO_SD_switch_rr6-nx to sdmc:/switch/rr6-nx. Extract your disc into game_root (not the ISO itself).
DLC is optional: put the packages under dlc/, in any folders. The first start then extracts about 1.9 GB next to your saves, so the
first boot takes longer and needs the space.

Which toml
----------
renut.toml        first run: shipped settings, logs on, CPU sampling on.
renut_play.toml   to play, diagnostics off.
renut_ab.toml     A/B: stay in one place for 10+ minutes, send logs/renut_001.log. Target 1 does nothing on the Switch: it is the control.

What to test, most important first
----------------------------------
1. Boot to a race. Logos, Pac-Man loader, title, World Xplorer, car select, first race.
2. Large wedge-shaped polygons in the race. Seen ONCE in the emulator: emu4, capture at lap 00:32, big flat streaked shapes each side of
   the road, over the rock wall on the first course. Not reproduced since, cause unknown. If you see them, note where, and whether
   rr6_depth_bias = false in renut.toml makes them go.
3. Overall brightness. banjo_renut_game_gamma is now on: the display's gamma ramp, which the reference applies and Renut did not. Menus went
   from 3 to 12 levels off the reference to under 1. In renut_ab.toml it is target 73: the off half is visibly brighter in the darks.
4. The car and glass. Still weaker than the reference: the rear window blotchy, the gloss on the car and the glow on bright buildings less.
   Known, not fixed yet.
5. Car at car select: should be textured. It was black until rr6_fog_nan_zero. Both worked in the emulator; confirm on hardware.
6. Foliage (trees beside the course). Flicker reported on the PC build, and the Switch's GPU is NVIDIA too. Under investigation: with the car
   braked and nothing else moving, 3 to 4 % of tree pixels still change from capture to capture. Watch for it.
7. Speed. The game slows down when frames run late: at about 38 fps in the emulator the lap clock ran at 0.755 of real time. It is not a
   strict one tick per frame. Compare the on-screen lap clock with a stopwatch in a race. The game's timing has not been changed.
8. Long stalls. The emulator had stretches under 3 fps around some loads and at the race's start, with no shader compiles: 3 to 7 windows of
   10 s in a run with the guard off, 7 to 12 with it on. Unknown whether this is the emulator. Note any stall on the console.
9. A dark scene with no car and the HUD bright, once in the emulator, while the car was stuck against the wall (emu11, capture 027). It looks
   like the game's own reset of a stuck car; not confirmed. Note it if you see it while driving normally.
10. Music: pick "Disc 4: Player Disc" under Change BGM, and race. Nobody has listened to this yet, on any platform. The largest pack
   (Silver Stream, 68.9 MB) opened and streamed on the PC.
11. Unlock keys: hidden by default. rr6_dlc_unlock_keys = true shows them; that is your decision.

Console profile
---------------
renut.toml has switch_profile_stacks = true. Play the slow scene for a few minutes and send logs/rex/rex_profile.log with rr6-nx.elf from
this package: a profile only maps with the ELF of the same build. Sampling pauses threads 1,000 times a second, so read shares from such a
run, not its best frame rate. Name the scene and the time.

Not in this package, by your order: PGO and LTO, hand-written natives (they need a console profile first).

Known problems, not fixed
-------------------------
- PC only: Renut on Vulkan draws the race wrongly (the car's far side shows through, large polygons over the scene). Direct3D 12 and
  deko3d do not. Looks like a depth or stencil problem. Cause not found.
- PC only: Direct3D 12 hung the GPU twice (device removed, 887A0006), both times with another heavy process running.
- Direct3D 12 applies rr6_depth_bias only with the Agility SDK.
